hits.text: Thresholding the Doublet Likelihood In principle, the doublet likelihood L(x) alone could be used to decide on which cells are putative doublets: if hLðxÞi>0:5, call a cell a doublet. The conﬁdence in the call is simply the value of L(x) itself. However, the doublet likelihood L(x) is sensitive to the prior guess, br, on the fraction of observed transcriptomes that are doublets. In practice br is known roughly, but it is easy to be off by several-fold from its true value r. Though uncertainty in br is already used to estimate the error in L(x)i n Equation 8, we should ideally look for a method of doublet classiﬁcation that is not sensitive to br. To do this, we treat L(x) as a feature on which to perform classiﬁcation, rather than as a strict posterior Bayesian probability.
